You are one of several READ-ONLY audit agents for the Nxeon customer-portal redesign (Phase 1 = audit only). Codebase: /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router, Prisma/Postgres, separate worker/ process). Customer portal = app/dashboard/** + components/customer/** + components/portal/**; API under app/api/**; logic in lib/**; schema in prisma/schema.prisma.

HARD RULES: STRICTLY READ-ONLY. Do NOT edit/create/delete ANY file under /opt/nxeon, /opt/nxeon-staging or /opt/nxeon-sandbox. No build, npm, prisma, db, git-write, or service commands. Do NOT touch the live database, Stripe, or infrastructure. Do not read .env* files. Your ONLY write is your report file: /tmp/claude-0/-root/1716c7ee-ae35-4cf5-b557-9059709e07c4/scratchpad/audit-06-account-billing-support.md (Write tool). Exhaustive, factual, cite repo-relative file paths, use tables, mark uncertain items UNVERIFIED. Purpose: 'nothing gets lost' capability safety net.

YOUR AUDIT: ACCOUNT-LEVEL capability inventory (SKIP domains and email — already audited). Areas:
1. DASHBOARD HOME (app/dashboard/page.tsx + components it renders, PortalHero): every widget, data source, conditional states (new user / has resources / attention items / promos / win-back banners / onboarding checklist), quick actions.
2. BILLING (app/dashboard/billing/**, invoices/**): balance/credits/wallet, payment methods (Stripe: cards, setup intents, default method), subscriptions list + actions (cancel/resume/change interval/upgrade), invoices (list/download PDF/pay overdue), transactions/ledger, credits/promo codes/coupons (COMEBACK50, first-month-free hosting-only, riddle $100), currency display (geoip display currency vs billing currency), VAT/tax handling, dunning/overdue states, auto-renew toggles, refunds, receipts emails. Cite each API route.
3. SETTINGS (app/dashboard/settings/**): profile, email change, password, 2FA/TOTP/passkeys, sessions/devices, API keys/tokens, notifications preferences, SSH keys (global), timezone/locale/currency, delete account, data export, connected accounts (Kodely SSO), preferences.
4. TEAM (app/dashboard/team/**): roles, invite flow, permissions matrix (which actions each role can do — find the permission-check helper and list all permission keys), ownership transfer, audit.
5. SUPPORT (app/dashboard/support/**): tickets (create fields, categories, priorities, attachments, replies, statuses), live chat widget (the AI chat agent — state, tool loop, degraded mode), knowledge base/docs links, status page, feedback (app/dashboard/feedback), the persistent support launcher in Shell.
6. ACTIVITY (app/dashboard/activity/**): event types logged (list the enum/source), filters, retention.
7. REFERRALS (refer/**), AFFILIATE (affiliate/**), PARTNER (partner/**): programs, commission logic, links/codes, payouts, stats, partner API keys (Kodely partner API), any dashboards.
8. WHAT'S NEW (whats-new/**), CALENDAR (calendar/**), NOTIFICATIONS (in-app notification centre if any, email notifications list — every transactional email the customer can receive, from lib/email* or emails/ dir, with trigger).
9. AUTH & ONBOARDING: login/signup/verify/reset/magic-link/OAuth/SSO routes and steps, onboarding after signup, session handling (only as it affects UI).
10. Global: currency switcher, locale/i18n (any?), theme toggle (light theme exists?), keyboard shortcuts, command palette actions relevant to account.
For each area: data models + enums; CAPABILITY TABLE (action | UI location | API route | backend fn | effect | danger | state handling | reversible | notes); feature flags; role gating; gaps (backend-not-in-UI, UI stubs).
Finish by writing the report, then reply with a ~12-line summary.

This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.

Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.

- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests).
